results.title: Will Higher Tariffs Affect Electric Vehicle Prices?
results.content:
Electric vehicles (EVs) often rely on global supply chains. When tariffs
increase, production costs can rise significantly, especially for EVs that
depend on non-domestic battery packs or advanced electronics.

## How Tariffs May Influence EV Prices

You may see price increases in areas such as:

Base Manufacturer’s Suggested Retail Price (MSRP)

Trims that include high-end technology packages

Battery-electric models built with internationally sourced parts [...] A tariff is a tax placed on imported goods. In 2025, the U.S. government
implemented new tariffs that directly impact the automotive industry. These
tariffs apply to:

Vehicles imported from countries without favorable trade
agreements

Automotive components, particularly EV batteries, semiconductors, and
electronic control modules [...] In today’s modern automotive market, partnering with a dealership that
truly understands the impacts of tariffs can make a world of difference. At
Toyota of Denton, we prioritize transparency and customer education so you
can make confident decisions, even when external factors like tariffs create
uncertainty. Our team continuously monitors changes in manufacturing
locations, import taxes, and incentives to provide you with real-time
guidance tailored to your needs.

results.title: New Modeling Shows How Much Auto Tariffs Will Raise Prices and Harm Buyers
results.content:
Total vehicle sales fall by about 3 percent to 6 percent.
 Electric vehicle sales decline by about 2 percent to 3 percent, while gas-powered vehicle sales fall by about 3 percent to 7 percent.
 Average vehicle prices rise by about 4 percent to 7 percent, or by about $2,000 to $3,500. The price of imported vehicles rises by about 13 percent to 14 percent, or about $6,200 to $6,700. [...] “Vehicle manufacturing is a global effort. While the United States is trying to bring manufacturing back to its shores, our analysis shows that this plan would hurt people looking to buy a new car. This analysis shows that policymakers need to consider the full scale of the tariff’s impacts, including how these tariffs affect consumers by pushing them into purchasing decisions they wouldn’t otherwise make.”

—Beia Spiller, RFF Fellow and Director of the Transportation Program [...] Last month, the Trump administration announced tariffs that target imported vehicles and automobile parts. New modeling from researchers at Resources for the Future (RFF) projects that the tariffs will reduce vehicle sales, raise both gas and electric vehicle prices, and modestly boost profits for US manufacturers.
